title: Experience Day Gifts for Families: What to Check First
description: Buying an experience day gift for a child or family? Check age and height limits, expiry, booking, weather and exchanges first, plus top ideas.
h1: Experience day gifts for families: what to check first
intro: An experience can be the gift they remember for years. A little checking before you buy makes sure it’s a happy memory, not a voucher stuck in a drawer.

image.alt: Hot air balloons rising over the landscape

cardText: Age limits, expiry, booking and weather, plus great family ideas.

blocks.title: Scout’s gift checklist
blocks.text: Read the small print as if you’re the one going: who can take part, where, when, and what happens if it rains.

sections.html:
• Ages and sizes: many experiences have minimum ages, heights or weight limits.
  • Locations: is there a venue within reach of the recipient?
  • Validity: vouchers usually expire. Check if you can extend or exchange, and whether there’s a fee.
  • Booking: do you book with the voucher company or the venue, and how far ahead are dates available?
  • Weather: outdoor experiences like balloon flights can be rescheduled several times.

• Animal encounters at zoos and farm parks.
  • Treetop adventure and climbing courses.
  • Behind-the-scenes tours, like the Harry Potter Studio Tour.
  • Theatre trips and family shows.
  • Junior driving experiences for older kids.

See our experience days guide for where to buy.

A shared experience, like a steam train ride or an afternoon tea with a zoo visit, makes a lovely gift for grandparents and grandchildren to do together. Look for flexible “choice” vouchers if you’re not sure what they’d pick.

faqs.q: Can I extend an expired experience voucher?
faqs.a: Some providers let you extend a voucher for a fee, others don’t. Check the terms before buying and note the expiry date.
